tagline: A small town in the southern Isan, home to the giant Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddha and quiet rice-field life
introHtml: Amnat Charoen is a small province that was split off from Ubon Ratchathani, and most people only pass through it on the way between Ubon and Mukdahan. But if you actually stop, you'll find a quiet, plain Isan town. What locals think of first is the giant Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddha at the Buddhist park in the middle of town — the province's main Buddha image, visible from far away. Around the edges of town there are forest temples, sandstone outcrops like Phu Sing–Phu Pha Phueng, and wide rice fields where farming is the main way of life. The food is proper Isan: som tam, larb, river fish, and homemade fermented dishes. If you like small towns without big crowds of tourists, Amnat Charoen is a slow, easy stop with a genuine Isan feel.
bestTime: November–February is coolest and most comfortable for getting around; in the late-rainy to early-cool season the rice fields turn a lovely green

highlights.name: Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang
highlights.blurb: The province's giant Buddha image at Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddhist Park in central Amnat Charoen — visible from far off and the first thing people think of when they hear the province's name.

highlights.name: Buddhist Park and Khao Dan Phra Bat Na Maet
highlights.blurb: A wide sandstone plateau around the Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang image, with rock formations and viewpoints over town. An easy place for an evening stroll to catch the breeze.

highlights.name: Phu Sing–Phu Pha Phueng Forest Park
highlights.blurb: A sandstone hill area in Chanuman district with rock terraces, caves, and viewpoints looking across toward the Mekong River. A go-to nature spot for locals.

highlights.name: Wat Tham Saeng Phet (Wat Sirimongkhon)
highlights.blurb: A forest temple on a sandstone hill outside town, with caves, Buddha images set in rock crevices, and a shady, quiet atmosphere. A place for meditation and making merit.

highlights.name: Local handwoven and khit textiles
highlights.blurb: Weaving villages in the province still hand-weave cotton and khit-pattern cloth with local designs. You can buy them as souvenirs straight from where they're made.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and bamboo-shoot soup — bold flavors you can find all over town and the everyday food of Amnat Charoen locals.

foodScene.name: River fish and grilled fish
foodScene.note: Fish from local rivers and ponds, grilled in salt, made into larb pla, or cooked in tom yam, eaten with sticky rice the local way.

foodScene.name: Homemade fermented dishes
foodScene.note: Pla som, pla ra, and local naem, fermented at home — the seasonings and side dishes at the heart of an Isan kitchen.

foodScene.name: Khao chi and grilled sticky rice
foodScene.note: Grilled sticky rice brushed with egg, a morning snack that's easy to find at markets and along the road in town.

foodScene.name: Seasonal mushrooms and wild vegetables
foodScene.note: In the rainy season, wild mushrooms and foraged vegetables from the fields show up at the fresh market, cooked into Isan-style curries and soups.

foodScene.name: Evening market in town
foodScene.note: An evening market that gathers Isan street food and snacks to graze on after dark at local prices.

foodScene.name: Small cafes in town
foodScene.note: A few new cafes are opening up in town for a coffee break between sights — quiet and easygoing, the way a small town is.

attractions.name: Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddhist Park
attractions.blurb: Home to the province's giant Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddha, set on a wide sandstone plateau — a spot for making merit and taking in views over town.

attractions.name: Wat Tham Saeng Phet
attractions.blurb: A forest temple on a sandstone hill with caves and Buddha images in rock crevices, shady and quiet on the edge of town.

attractions.name: Phu Sing–Phu Pha Phueng Forest Park
attractions.blurb: A sandstone hill in Chanuman district with rock terraces, caves, and viewpoints toward the Mekong River — good for an easy walk in nature.

attractions.name: Lam Sebai Dam
attractions.blurb: A wide reservoir in the province with water and mountain views — a local spot for relaxing, fishing, and catching the evening light.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Lao Thep Nimit
attractions.blurb: An old temple in Phana district, home to the Phra Lao Thep Nimit, an ancient Buddha image long revered by locals — an important temple for the province.

attractions.name: Amnat Charoen town center
attractions.blurb: A small, quiet town with markets, Isan restaurants, and cafes to wander, good for a stop along the Ubon–Mukdahan route.

attractions.name: Local weaving villages
attractions.blurb: Communities that weave cotton and khit-pattern cloth with local designs in the province — watch the hand-weaving and pick up souvenirs at the source.

attractions.name: Rice fields and farming life around town
attractions.blurb: Wide rice paddies around the province; in the late-rainy to early-cool season the fields turn lush green — good for photos and seeing rural Isan life.
